entry._note: Respecified 2026-08-29 because the previous entry was not reachable by any order type. It filled at the order block's high the instant a bar's low touched it; smc_fill_model showed a limit resting there fills 31-42% of signals and almost only when the setup is failing, while a market order sent once the touch is known measured 48-79 bps of slippage against a 17.3 bps median stop distance. fill='next_open' scores the entry at the open of the bar AFTER the closed bar that produced the signal, which is what the live bot's market order actually gets; the live bot realises it by evaluating closed bars only (smc_cycle.closed_bars_only) and ordering at market immediately. require_ob_reclaim adds the one signal-side rule the fill model paid for: the retesting bar must CLOSE back above the OB high, which is decidable before the order goes in. Out-of-sample over 3 expanding folds, this spec beats no-reclaim on every cost basis (zero-cost +21.3% pf 2.02 vs +14.2% pf 1.60; with commission +20.2% vs +12.9%). See smc_entry_spec_results.csv.
entry._early_retest_note: Added 2026-08-31. A block retested at ob_idx+1 cannot be known to be valid then: the FVG that validates it is a three-candle pattern ending at ob_idx+2, so the backtest was reading a bar out of the future to score those entries. They were the whole of the 46% live/backtest signal gap -- all 68 missed signals were ob_idx+1 retests, all 57 agreed ones were older. 'skip' does not trade them, which is what the live bot has always done; it changes no live behaviour, only what the backtest is allowed to claim. 'defer' waits for the third candle and orders from there -- reachable, roughly doubles the trade count, and measured worse (see smc_full_backtest_results_defer.csv).

exit._note: Respecified 2026-08-29, same defect as the entry: each exit booked its own trigger as its fill. new_high_exit was the worst thing in the strategy -- it fires only once a swing high is CONFIRMED, which takes swing_window (20) bars, then filled at that pivot bar's own close, so it sold at a local peak with 100 minutes of hindsight. fill='next_open' prices each leg at what its own order type gets: the stop keeps its level because it rests at IBKR and triggers intrabar (but a bar that OPENS through it now fills at that open), while tp1, new_high_exit and same_day_force_close fill on the bar after the closed bar that revealed them, which is what the bot's market orders actually get. No live change was needed -- the bot already did all of this; the backtest was the thing that was wrong. Out-of-sample this cuts the zero-cost figure from +21.3% to +9.5% (the hindsight) while RAISING the measured-slippage figure from -1.8% to +6.1% (the 64 bps blanket was over-charging legs whose delay is now read off the bars), and the three cost bases converge instead of diverging. tp1_resting_limit models a bracketed take-profit resting at the target, which the bot does NOT have; measured at +5.8% OOS against +6.1% without it, so the OCA plumbing is not worth building. Keep it false unless that order is actually placed -- setting it true without building it puts the backtest back to scoring fills nobody gets. See smc_exit_spec_results.csv.

reactive_derisk._note: Confirmed inert over the most recent ~1yr walk-forward (2025-07 to 2026-07, clean full-SP500 re-sweep): trailing PF never dropped below pf_threshold in any fold on the CURRENT (post-d94a548) codebase, so this never triggered and made exactly 0.00pp difference vs no-derisk baseline in every fold's fit AND test period. Re-validated 2026-08-12 after discovering the prior v3 sweep (window=100, pf_threshold=0.8/1.2, size_mult=0.1) predated the 2026-08-09 entry-sizing fix (commit d94a548, post-TP1-mutated stop vs initial_stop_price) by only 4 minutes -- v4 re-ran the same walk-forward structure on the fixed code (profit factor ~3.3-4.95 vs v3's stale ~2.9-5.4) and reached the same qualitative conclusion. Note v4's own grid-search picks (window=200 in all 3 folds, matching this config's window below; pf_threshold=0.6, size_mult=0.1) aren't meaningfully validated beyond 'derisk never fired' -- any untriggered combo scores identically, so the specific pf_threshold/size_mult values below are still from the earlier fixed-years grid sweep, not this walk-forward. Kept as a starting point for a genuinely bad stretch (the scenario it was designed for), not because it's been proven to help -- see git history around commit d94a548 and smc_engine.simulate_smc_portfolio's docstring for the original tuning caveats.

time_filter._note: latest_entry_et moved 15:30 -> 15:45 on 2026-08-29. Of seven candidate windows swept at the full live basis (smc_entry_window_results.csv), this was the only change that held up: it beat 10:05-15:30 in 3 of 3 walk-forward folds on both cost bases, and a fit-period selection picked it in all 3, so fit and test agree. It is small -- 25 extra signals and 8 extra round trips over fourteen months, +0.18pp out of sample -- and it is free, needing no schedule change: the cycle already runs to the close, and get_market_status gates on this value alone. Widening the EARLY bound looked worth far more (+1.0pp at 09:45) and was rejected: it wins only 2 of 3 folds and no fit period ever selected it, which is a regime effect rather than an edge. Note it would also need the hardcoded 10:00 'too_early' floor in smc_live.get_market_status lifted, not just the two schedule changes. Mechanics of this bound: cycles fire at :x2/:x7 and act on the last CLOSED bar, so 15:45 admits the 15:42 cycle acting on the 15:35 bar, which fills at the 15:40 bar's open and is force-closed at 15:51 -- about fifteen minutes to work.
